Linkin Park is an American rock band formed in Agoura Hills, California, in 1996. The band's current lineup consists of vocalist/rhythm guitarist/keyboardist Mike Shinoda, lead guitarist Brad Delson, DJ/turntablist Joe Hahn, bassist Dave Farrell, vocalist Emily Armstrong, and drummer Colin Brittain. The lineup for the band's first seven studio albums included lead vocalist Chester Bennington and drummer Rob Bourdon; after Bennington's suicide in July 2017, the band endured a seven-year hiatus, during which Bourdon chose to depart from the band. In September 2024, Linkin Park's reformation was announced along with the addition of Armstrong and Brittain.
Categorized mainly as alternative rock and nu metal, Linkin Park's earlier music spanned a fusion of heavy metal and hip-hop, with their later music featuring more electronica and pop elements. The band rose to international fame with their debut studio album, Hybrid Theory (2000), which became certified Diamond by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). Released during the peak of the nu metal scene, the album's heavy airplay on MTV led to the singles "One Step Closer", "Crawling", and "In the End" all charting highly on the US Mainstream Rock chart. The lattermost also crossed over to the number two spot on the nation's Billboard Hot 100. The band's second album, Meteora (2003), continued in Hybrid Theory's footsteps, while their third album, Minutes to Midnight (2007), marked a change in sound. By the end of the decade, Linkin Park was among the most successful and popular rock acts.
The band continued to explore a wider variation of musical types on their fourth album, A Thousand Suns (2010), layering their music with more electronic sounds. The band's fifth album, Living Things (2012), combined musical elements from all of their previous records. Their sixth album, The Hunting Party (2014), returned to a heavier alternative metal/rock sound, while their seventh album, One More Light (2017), was a substantially more pop/pop rock-oriented record. The band's eighth album, From Zero (2024), once again returned to a heavier, more stylistically diverse sound.

Linkin Park is one of the best-selling music acts of all time, having sold over 100 million records worldwide. They have won two Grammy Awards, seven American Music Awards, four Billboard Music Awards, four MTV Video Music Awards, 10 MTV Europe Music Awards, and three World Music Awards. In 2003, MTV2 named Linkin Park the sixth-greatest band of the music video era and the third-best of the new millennium. Billboard ranked Linkin Park No. 19 on the Best Artists of the Decade list. In 2012, the band was voted as the greatest artist of the 2000s in a Bracket Madness poll on VH1. In 2014, the band was declared "the Biggest Rock Band in the World Right Now" by Kerrang!.
History  
Foundation and early years (1996–2000)

Linkin Park was founded by three high school friends: Mike Shinoda, Rob Bourdon, and Brad Delson.[1] The three attended Agoura High School in Agoura Hills, California, a suburb of Los Angeles.[1] After graduating from high school, the three began to take their musical interests more seriously, recruiting Joe Hahn, Dave "Phoenix" Farrell, and Mark Wakefield to perform in their band, then called Xero. Though limited in resources, the band began recording and producing songs within Shinoda's makeshift bedroom studio in 1996, resulting in a four-track demo album, entitled Xero, released in November 1997.[1] That same month, the band performed their first show, opening for SX-10 and System of a Down at the Whisky a Go Go, a nightclub in West Hollywood.[2] Delson introduced the band to Jeff Blue, the vice president of A&R for Zomba Music, whom he had interned for in college.[3] Blue offered the band constructive criticism to catch the attention of record labels. Blue himself was impressed with Xero after watching them play a live show in 1998, but believed the band needed a different vocalist.[3] Tensions and frustration within the band grew after they failed to land a record deal.[1] The lack of success and stalemate in progress prompted Wakefield, at that time the band's vocalist, to leave the band in search of other projects.[1] Farrell also left to tour with Tasty Snax, a Christian punk and ska band.[4][5]

**Musicians that also design Album Covers – A Fairly-Comprehensive List for Fans of Music and Art**
by Mike Goldstein, curator, AlbumCoverHallofFame.com
originally posted March 15, 2013 (updated June, 2026)
There are many examples of musical artists who are also accomplished visual artists, displaying great talent in the fields of painting, illustration, photography, sculpture and product design. Scholars of rock musicians know that a number of well-known musical acts were founded by art students that met each other while attending art school. Examples include Pink Floyd (Roger Waters, Nick Mason and Richard Wright all went to London’s Polytechnic College on Regent Street, while Syd Barrett studied at Camberwell), Talking Heads (David Byrne, Tina Weymouth and Chris Frantz all attended the Rhode Island School of Design), Devo (Mark Mothersbaugh and Jerry Casale studied at Kent State) and The Clash (Joe Strummer, Paul Simonon and Mick Jones). Other well-known musicians who studied art include Queen’s Freddie Mercury (who attended both Isleworth Polytechnic and Ealing College and who went on to design the famous “Queen Crest”), Eric Clapton (Kingston College of Art), Pete Townshend (another Ealing alumnus), Brian Eno (Winchester Art School), R.E.M.’s Michael Stipe (a U. of Georgia art major), Ray Davies of The Kinks (Hornsey College of Art in London ), Keith Richards (London’s Sidcup Art College) and Ron Wood (Ealing again) of The Rolling Stones and John Lennon (Liverpool College of Art). After studying art at the University of Newcastle upon Tyne under the tutelage of Richard Hamilton, Roxy Music’s Bryan Ferry had a career as high school art instructor – specializing in ceramics and pottery – prior to forming the band in late 1970.
Whatever their motivations (Mick Jones of The Clash is quoted as saying that, although he felt that he had no real artistic talent, he went to art school to form a band, as had many of his musical influences – Lennon, Richards, Townshend, etc. – who’d gone to art school and then formed bands soon after), it is clear that right-brained, multi-talented individuals seem to have had an important influence on the development of both the aural and visual aspects of the pop music business.

The following are some examples of musicians who’ve also demonstrated their graphical skills in creating imagery used on some of their best-known album covers:

https://josepharthur.com/originalart/
**Martin Atkins** – drummer/producer – PiL, NIN, Killing Joke, Pigface, Ministry and others – Pigface – _Notes From Thee Underground_ and _Feels Like Heaven_; The Damage Manual – _Limited Edition_ and _>1_ (Artwork, Art Direction)
https://martinatkins.com/
**Sam Beam** – multi-instrumentalist – Iron & Wine – Iron & Wine – _The Creek Drank the Cradle, Kiss Each Other Clean_ and _Around The Well_ (Paintings, Illustrations, Art Direction)
https://ironandwine.com/about/
**Tony Bennett** – singer – Rosemary Clooney – _Girl Singer_; Tony Bennett – _Perfectly Frank_; Bill Evans – _Blue In Green_; Leonard Feather – _Night Blooming_ (Paintings released under his given name, Anthony Benedetto)
https://tonybennett.com/benedetto_arts.php
**David Byrne** – singer/guitarist/songwriter – Talking Heads – Talking Heads – _Talking Heads, Naked, Stop Making Sense, Speaking In Tongues, More Songs About Buildings And Food_ and _Talking Heads 77;_ Fatboy Slim – _Here Lies Love;_ David Byrne – _Forest_ and _Big Love_ (Photography, Graphic Design)
https://davidbyrne.com
**Michael Cartellone** – drummer, Lynyrd Skynyrd – Lynyrd Skynyrd – _Lynyrd Skynyrd Greatest Hits_ (Paintings)
http://www.michaelcartellone.com
**Wayne Coyne** – singer/guitarist, The Flaming Lips – The Flaming Lips – _Telepathic Surgery_ and _Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots_ (Paintings)
https://waynecoyneartshop.com

**Bob Dylan** – singer/songwriter – Bob Dylan – _Self Portrait_ (Painting)
https://www.bobdylan.com/
**John Entwistle** – bass guitarist, The Who – The Who – _The Who By Numbers_ (Drawings)
https://artofrockandroll.com/john-entwistle/

https://portugaltheman.com/?frontpage=true

**Musicians that also design Album Covers – A Fairly-Comprehensive List for Fans of Music and Art**
by Mike Goldstein, curator, AlbumCoverHallofFame.com
originally posted March 15, 2013 (updated June, 2026)
There are many examples of musical artists who are also accomplished visual artists, displaying great talent in the fields of painting, illustration, photography, sculpture and product design. Scholars of rock musicians know that a number of well-known musical acts were founded by art students that met each other while attending art school. Examples include Pink Floyd (Roger Waters, Nick Mason and Richard Wright all went to London’s Polytechnic College on Regent Street, while Syd Barrett studied at Camberwell), Talking Heads (David Byrne, Tina Weymouth and Chris Frantz all attended the Rhode Island School of Design), Devo (Mark Mothersbaugh and Jerry Casale studied at Kent State) and The Clash (Joe Strummer, Paul Simonon and Mick Jones). Other well-known musicians who studied art include Queen’s Freddie Mercury (who attended both Isleworth Polytechnic and Ealing College and who went on to design the famous “Queen Crest”), Eric Clapton (Kingston College of Art), Pete Townshend (another Ealing alumnus), Brian Eno (Winchester Art School), R.E.M.’s Michael Stipe (a U. of Georgia art major), Ray Davies of The Kinks (Hornsey College of Art in London ), Keith Richards (London’s Sidcup Art College) and Ron Wood (Ealing again) of The Rolling Stones and John Lennon (Liverpool College of Art). After studying art at the University of Newcastle upon Tyne under the tutelage of Richard Hamilton, Roxy Music’s Bryan Ferry had a career as high school art instructor – specializing in ceramics and pottery – prior to forming the band in late 1970.
Whatever their motivations (Mick Jones of The Clash is quoted as saying that, although he felt that he had no real artistic talent, he went to art school to form a band, as had many of his musical influences – Lennon, Richards, Townshend, etc. – who’d gone to art school and then formed bands soon after), it is clear that right-brained, multi-talented individuals seem to have had an important influence on the development of both the aural and visual aspects of the pop music business.
